decisions.decision: Use scheduled batch scoring for document classification
decisions.context: The system processes millions of documents daily, with seasonal volume changes. The brief does not require immediate predictions for each incoming document.
decisions.rationale: Batch scoring fits the stated high volume without an unstated real-time requirement. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2” and “Three Levels of ML Software” describe scheduled batch prediction deployment.
consequences: Choose a scoring cadence that meets operational freshness needs.
Persist results where consuming teams can access them.
Plan capacity for seasonal processing peaks.

decisions.decision: Scale classification resources elastically with demand
decisions.context: Incoming volume varies strongly over the year, so fixed capacity risks either peak-period bottlenecks or idle capacity.

alternatives.label: Vertically scalable training
cons: Does not directly address variable serving load

decisions.rationale: Elastic scaling matches the seasonal workload pattern. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2” and “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” discuss scaling resources with workload demand.
consequences: Define scaling thresholds and maximum capacity.
Track utilization and processing backlog across seasons.
Validate scaling behavior against peak volume.

decisions.decision: Expose classification results through a REST prediction microservice
decisions.context: Several teams consume the classification results, so the system needs a common integration boundary. The brief does not specify a required client protocol.

alternatives.label: REST prediction microservice
cons: Batch result access still needs a delivery contract

alternatives.label: gRPC model interface
cons: Less directly grounded for batch consumers

decisions.rationale: A REST interface gives consuming teams a shared integration point; pair it with persisted batch results for scheduled scoring. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2” and “Three Levels of ML Software” describe API-backed prediction services.
consequences: Specify a stable request and result schema.
Coordinate service access and version changes across teams.
Clarify whether consumers read stored results or submit requests.

decisions.decision: Monitor input drift and prediction quality in production
decisions.context: Operators need visibility into quality drift. Inputs may shift before delayed labels make prediction quality measurable, so monitoring should cover both signals.

alternatives.label: Input and feature-drift monitoring
cons: Drift does not prove quality loss

decisions.rationale: Use input drift as the primary early signal and add quality monitoring where labels become available; the monitoring dimension has low exclusivity, so these practices can be combined. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “Machine Learning Monitoring: What It Is, and What We Are Missing” discuss drift and quality monitoring.
consequences: Retain suitable input statistics for comparison.
Set thresholds and an investigation process.
Connect delayed labels to later quality assessment.

uncovered: LLM provider, model selection, and prompt or model versioning.
Label acquisition and ground-truth timing for quality measurement.
Classification accuracy targets and drift alert thresholds.
Privacy, retention, and access controls for insurance documents.
Batch cadence, freshness objectives, and backlog recovery targets.
Result storage, ownership, and delivery contracts for consuming teams.

Human review and escalation for uncertain or consequential classifications. Design-point checks were novel and unattested: the proposed combination returned no attested sources or warnings; a rival combination using queued online serving, vertically scalable training, and passive operation was also unattested.
